metadata.title: ORECH/DIN | Boutique Law Office in Antwerp, Belgium
metadata.description: ORECH/DIN is a boutique law office in Antwerp assisting individuals, entrepreneurs and businesses with legal matters in Belgium, including clients from abroad.

hero.title: Legal assistance when it matters the most.
hero.intro: ORECH/DIN advises and represents individuals, entrepreneurs and businesses in legal matters in Belgium. With more than 25 years of experience each, our lawyers combine broad legal knowledge with personal involvement, clear communication and a focused approach.
hero.supporting: When your rights or interests are at stake, we stand by you and act with determination.
hero.imageAlt: Belgian chambers interior, bookcase, antique desk lamp and a view onto the Antwerp Grote Markt

personal.title: Personal attention, backed by experience.
personal.p1: Every legal matter starts with listening. We take the time to understand and analyse your situation, what matters to you and what you want to achieve.
personal.p2: Your matter is handled by either Nir Zeltzer or Deborah Johnson, both with more than 25 years of experience. That experience is combined with continuous professional training and a broad legal knowledge base.
personal.p3: Where additional expertise is useful, we can rely on a broad professional network.

items.title: Business & Commercial Matters
items.body: Advice and representation in business and commercial matters, including contracts, debt recovery and unpaid invoices.

items.title: Property, Construction & Rental Matters
items.body: Legal assistance concerning property, construction and rental matters.

items.title: Criminal & Traffic Matters
items.body: Assistance and representation in criminal and traffic matters.

items.title: Civil Matters & Liability
items.body: Civil matters and disputes, including liability, insurance matters and accidents.

items.title: Private & Family Matters
items.body: Assistance with private and family matters, including divorce.

advice.title: Advice, negotiation and representation
advice.p1: Not every legal problem needs to end in court. We assess the legal position and the practical options, discuss the strategy with you and act accordingly.
advice.p2: Where a settlement can appropriately resolve the matter, we will seek to achieve it. Where proceedings are necessary, we prepare the case carefully and represent your interests firmly.

abroad.title: Legal matters in Belgium, also for clients abroad.
abroad.p1: ORECH/DIN focuses on legal matters in Belgium. We also assist clients living or operating abroad who need legal assistance or a reliable legal contact in Belgium.
abroad.p2: Meetings can take place at our office in Antwerp or online.

contact.title: Speak to us.
contact.p1: If you have a legal question or are facing a dispute, you can contact ORECH/DIN directly.
contact.p2: Call the office, send us an email or send us a short enquiry.
contact.p3: Meetings can take place at our office in Antwerp or online.

metadata.title: Our Lawyers
metadata.description: Nir Zeltzer and Deborah Johnson each bring more than 25 years of experience and a personal, practical approach to ORECH/DIN in Antwerp.

LawyersPage.title: Two experienced lawyers. One personal approach.

intro.p1: Nir Zeltzer and Deborah Johnson each bring more than 25 years of experience and their own areas of expertise to ORECH/DIN.
intro.p2: Their work is built on trust, personal involvement, practical thinking and a clear understanding of what is important to clients.
intro.p3: Continuous professional training ensures that this experience is supported by up-to-date legal knowledge.

nir.name: Nir Zeltzer
paragraphs: With more than 25 years of experience, Nir Zeltzer combines broad legal knowledge with a personal, practical and solution-focused approach.

His legal background is complemented by a diploma in Real Estate Expertise, providing additional technical insight in property-related matters, as well as a Master in Business Law from the University of Antwerp.

He approaches matters analytically and with a strong focus on your objectives. Careful analysis and trust are central to the way he works. Where a matter calls for more than a standard legal answer, he is prepared to think outside the box and draw on a broad range of legal sources, professional contacts and networks to identify a practical way forward.

He has extensive experience in negotiation and conflict resolution, including complex matters and situations requiring decisions under pressure. Depending on the circumstances, this may involve advising behind the scenes, negotiating towards a workable solution or taking a clear position in court when necessary.
He remains closely involved throughout the matter, explains the available options and helps you make informed decisions with a clear focus on the result to be achieved.
education: Master in Business Law, Antwerp University

deborah.name: Deborah Johnson
paragraphs: Deborah Johnson is an experienced litigator who combines firm representation in court with a calm, structured and carefully prepared approach.

With more than 25 years of experience, she knows that clients often need more than a legal answer: they need to understand what is happening, what the options are and what to expect next. She keeps matters organised, explains the process clearly and remains closely involved throughout the case.
She has also completed a specialised training in cassation proceedings in criminal cases (bijzondere opleiding cassatieprocedure in strafzaken).
She approaches each matter with depth and insight, while maintaining a professional and human approach that clients value highly.
Trust, thorough preparation and a clear sense of direction are central to the way she works, both in negotiations and in court.
education: Specialised training in cassation proceedings in criminal cases (bijzondere opleiding cassatieprocedure in strafzaken)

metadata.title: Practice Areas
metadata.description: ORECH/DIN assists individuals, entrepreneurs and businesses with legal matters in Belgium: business and commercial, property and construction, criminal and traffic, civil and liability, and private and family matters.

ServicesPage.title: Practice Areas

intro.p1: ORECH/DIN assists individuals, entrepreneurs and businesses with legal matters in Belgium.
intro.p2: Whether the issue concerns a contract, a commercial dispute, property, liability, a family matter or proceedings before a court, we first take the time to understand and analyse the situation, explain the available options and determine the appropriate way forward.
intro.p3: Our lawyers each bring more than 25 years of experience, combined with a practical and personal approach and close attention to what is at stake for you.

areas.title: Business & Commercial Matters
areas.p1: Legal issues can quickly become a distraction from running a business. We assist with contracts, commercial disputes, unpaid invoices and debt recovery, and help you find a clear way forward.
areas.p2: We also step in when your business interests, contractual rights or financial position are being challenged. Where possible, we work towards a practical solution. Whether proceedings are necessary or you are summoned to court, we prepare thoroughly to pursue your rights and defend your interests before the courts.

areas.title: Property, Construction & Rental Matters
areas.p1: Property, construction and rental matters can quickly become complex, particularly where contractual, technical and financial issues overlap. We help you understand your position, address disputes and find a practical way forward.
areas.p2: Our work includes property and construction disputes, rental matters and other conflicts relating to real estate, with attention to both the legal position and the practical consequences for you. Where court proceedings are required, we represent you and protect your interests throughout the process.

areas.title: Criminal & Traffic Matters
areas.p1: Criminal and traffic matters can leave people feeling overwhelmed, uncertain or unsure how to respond. We stand by you, explain the situation and the procedure clearly, and help you understand the choices that need to be made.
areas.p2: We remain closely involved throughout the matter, while keeping you informed and involved in the decisions. Where representation is required, we defend your interests before the police, prosecution authorities and courts, with attention to both the legal position and the practical consequences.

areas.title: Civil Matters & Liability
areas.p1: Accidents, liability issues and insurance disputes can have an immediate impact on a person’s daily life, finances or business. We help you understand where you stand, what can reasonably be claimed or defended, and which steps are available.
areas.p2: We assist with civil disputes, liability claims, insurance matters and accidents, keeping you informed and involved throughout the process. Where court proceedings are required, we pursue your rights or defend your interests carefully.

areas.title: Private & Family Matters
areas.p1: Private and family matters can be frustrating, emotionally demanding and difficult to navigate, especially when important personal decisions, practical consequences and sometimes children are involved. We help you understand your legal position and the available options, while keeping the process clear and manageable.
areas.p2: We assist with divorce and other private or family-related matters, with attention to both the legal and personal impact of the situation. Our role is to provide clear guidance, protect your position and help you move through what can be a deeply difficult or even traumatic period with as much certainty and control as possible.

ServicesPage.litigation: When a matter cannot be resolved outside court, we are prepared to act. Whether proceedings are necessary or you are summoned to court, we prepare thoroughly to pursue your rights and defend your interests firmly before the courts.

metadata.title: The Office
metadata.description: ORECH/DIN is a boutique law office in Antwerp. We assist individuals, entrepreneurs and businesses with legal matters in Belgium, through advice, negotiation and representation when needed.

intro.p1: Legal issues can quickly become frustrating, overwhelming or difficult to assess. Sometimes what is needed first is clear, reliable advice and a sense of what the next step should be.
intro.p2: At ORECH/DIN, we start by understanding the situation, what is at stake and what you want to achieve. From there, we determine the appropriate legal and practical approach.
intro.p3: As a boutique law office based in Antwerp, we assist individuals, entrepreneurs and businesses with legal matters in Belgium. Our lawyers each bring more than 25 years of experience, combined with personal involvement, trust and a practical way of working.
intro.p4: We help you assert and protect your rights through advice, negotiation and settlement where appropriate, and through representation before the courts when proceedings are necessary.
intro.p5: Where additional expertise is useful, we can rely on a broad professional network.

direct.p2: For individuals, entrepreneurs and businesses alike, we focus on clear legal advice and consultation, efficient handling and practical decisions that protect what matters.
direct.p3: Meetings can take place at our office in Antwerp or online.

metadata.title: Cookie policy
metadata.description: Which cookies orechdin.be places, why, how long they last, and how to refuse or withdraw your consent.

CookiePage.headline: Cookie policy
CookiePage.intro: This policy explains what is stored on your device when you visit this website, why, and how you keep control of it. It applies to www.orechdin.be and follows Article 129 of the Belgian Act of 13 June 2005 on electronic communications, the General Data Protection Regulation and the Belgian Data Protection Act of 30 July 2018.
CookiePage.summaryBody: This website uses two small items that are strictly necessary: a record of your cookie choice and a record of your language choice. The only optional item is the Google Maps frame on the contact page, which loads only if you allow it. There are no analytics, no advertising and no social media cookies.
CookiePage.whatBody1: A cookie is a small file a website asks your browser to keep. The law is broader than the word suggests: it covers any storing or reading of information on your device. Local storage and session storage are therefore covered by the same rules. This website uses neither.
CookiePage.whatBody2: Items placed by orechdin.be itself are first party. Items placed by another company through content we embed are third party, and that company decides what it does with them.
CookiePage.basisBody1: Storage that is strictly necessary for a service you asked for does not require consent, and switching it off would break the site. Everything else requires your prior, free and specific permission.
CookiePage.basisBody2: So we ask before placing anything optional, never in advance, and we never treat continued browsing as agreement. Refusing takes one click, exactly like accepting, and has no effect on your access to any part of this website. Your answer is kept for six months, after which we ask again.
CookiePage.registerIntro: Everything this website can store on your device, with its purpose, who can read it and how long it lasts.
CookiePage.emptyCategory: Nothing in this category is in use on this website at the moment. If that changes, it will be listed here and will load only after you have allowed it.

consent.purpose: Stores the cookie choice you made, so we do not ask again on every page and can show what you agreed to.

googleMaps.purpose: Placed by Google when you choose to load the map on the contact page. Google receives your IP address and uses these cookies for its own purposes, including security and, depending on your Google settings, personalisation.
googleMaps.duration: Determined by Google, see Google policy

locale.purpose: Remembers which language you are reading the site in, so every page stays in that language.

CookiePage.thirdPartyBody1: Google Maps is the only external service this website can contact, only on the contact page, and only after you have allowed it. Until then the map is replaced by a placeholder and no request reaches Google. If you never allow it, Google is never told that you visited this site.
CookiePage.thirdPartyBody2: What Google does with the data it receives is governed by its own policy:
CookiePage.secrecyBody: As an advocate this firm is bound by professional secrecy under Article 458 of the Criminal Code. None of the items above touch the substance of a case: no cookie on this website records who you are, what you are seeking advice about, or anything you write to us. That duty of confidence is why this site carries no advertising, no social media pixels and no third party analytics.
CookiePage.browserBody: Independently of the choice you make here, your browser can block or delete cookies for every site you visit. Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari all have these controls in their settings, in the privacy section. Blocking strictly necessary items may stop parts of this website from working.
CookiePage.complaintBody1: Questions about this policy go to {name}, at
CookiePage.complaintBody2: If our answer does not satisfy you, you may complain to the Belgian Data Protection Authority (Gegevensbeschermingsautoriteit) at
CookiePage.closing: This policy is republished with a new version number whenever the register above changes, and earlier versions are kept, so it stays possible to establish what applied on a given date.
CookiePage.whatBody3: Cookies also differ in how long they last. A session cookie disappears when you close your browser. A persistent cookie stays until it expires or you delete it.
CookiePage.linksBody: The Call, Email and WhatsApp buttons and the directions link are ordinary links. Nothing is loaded from WhatsApp or Google until you click one, and this website sets no cookie when you do.

metadata.title: Privacy statement
metadata.description: How ORECH/DIN handles personal data: whose data, why, on what legal basis, who receives it, how long it is kept, your rights, and how professional secrecy affects them.

PrivacyPage.headline: Privacy statement
PrivacyPage.intro: This statement explains how ORECH/DIN handles personal data: that of visitors to this website, of people who contact the office, of clients, and of other people involved in a client’s matter. It follows Articles 13 and 14 of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the Belgian Data Protection Act of 30 July 2018. Personal data means any information about an identifiable person, such as a name, an address or a description of a situation.
PrivacyPage.controllerBody1: The controller is {name}, a private limited company (BV) at {street}, {postal} {city}, Belgium, registered under company number {kbo} and entered in the {court}.
PrivacyPage.controllerBody2: For anything concerning personal data you can contact {name} directly, at
PrivacyPage.secrecyBody1: An advocate is bound by professional secrecy under Article 458 of the Criminal Code. What a client or a prospective client tells the office is confidential, and that duty does not end when the file closes.
PrivacyPage.secrecyBody2: This shapes your data protection rights. Where answering a request would reveal information covered by professional secrecy, in particular information belonging to another person involved in a case, the office must decline to disclose it. In that situation we tell you that the request has been limited, and explain why as far as secrecy allows.
PrivacyPage.secrecyBody3: Inside the office, files are open only to the people who need them for the work, and the duty of secrecy applies to everyone who works for the office.
PrivacyPage.whoHeading: Whose data, and where it comes from
PrivacyPage.whoIntro: The office processes personal data of:
PrivacyPage.whoVisitorsBody: Technical data that every website receives when a page is requested.
PrivacyPage.whoEnquirersBody: By the contact form, email, telephone or WhatsApp.
PrivacyPage.whoClientsBody: People whose matters the office handles or may handle.
PrivacyPage.whoOthersBody: Such as opposing parties, their lawyers, witnesses, experts and relatives named in documents.
PrivacyPage.whoSources: Most data comes from you. The rest comes from public sources and registers, from courts and public authorities, from other lawyers and professionals, and from the documents in a case.
PrivacyPage.dataIntro: Depending on who you are, the following:
PrivacyPage.dataVisitBody: Your IP address and technical request data (the page asked for, the time, the type of browser), processed by our hosting provider to deliver the pages and keep the service secure. We keep no visitor analytics.
PrivacyPage.dataContactBody: The name, email address, telephone number and description of your matter that you choose to send through the contact form, by email or by telephone. The form reaches the office by email and is not stored on the website. To limit abuse, it applies short-lived technical limits per address, which are not linked to your message.
PrivacyPage.dataWhatsappBody: If you write to the office on WhatsApp, WhatsApp (Meta) also processes your number and your message under its own terms. For anything confidential, please call or email instead.
PrivacyPage.dataClientBody: Identification and contact details, a copy of your identity document where the law requires it, bank details for payments and refunds, and everything you tell us or hand us about your matter, together with the invoices and correspondence in the file.
PrivacyPage.dataOthersBody: Name, role in the matter and the information found in the documents of the case, to the extent needed to act for the client.
PrivacyPage.dataSpecialBody: A file can contain health data, data about minors, or data about offences and convictions. The office processes these only where the matter needs it.
PrivacyPage.purposesHeading: Why, and on what legal basis
PrivacyPage.purposesIntro: Each purpose rests on one of the grounds in Article 6 GDPR:
PrivacyPage.basisContractBody: Answering your enquiry, assessing whether we can act for you, carrying out the work once we do, and invoicing it.
PrivacyPage.basisLegalBody: Identification and record keeping under the anti money laundering rules, accounting and tax duties, and the professional rules of the Bar.
PrivacyPage.basisInterestBody: Keeping the website secure and available, checking for conflicts of interest, recovering fees, and establishing or defending legal claims, including our own. It also covers acting for a client against another person, whose data we then process as far as the matter requires.
PrivacyPage.basisConsentBody: Optional cookies. You may withdraw consent at any time, without affecting what was done before.
PrivacyPage.basisSpecialLabel: Special categories and criminal data, Articles 9 and 10.
PrivacyPage.basisSpecialBody: A file may contain health data, or data about offences and convictions. The office processes these where necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims, the ground Article 9(2)(f) provides for legal work.
PrivacyPage.cookiesBody: This website stores only what is necessary unless you allow more. What is stored, why, and how to withdraw permission is set out in the
PrivacyPage.marketingBody: The office does not send newsletters or marketing messages. If it ever contacts former clients about its services or about legal developments, it will do so only where the law allows, and you can object at any time, free of charge.
PrivacyPage.recipientsBody1: The office does not sell personal data and does not share it for anyone else’s marketing. Data goes only to:
PrivacyPage.recipientHostingBody: Vercel Inc., a US company, which serves the website from servers in Frankfurt, as a processor.
PrivacyPage.recipientMailBody: Easyhost, which hosts the office’s email and carries messages sent from and to the office, as a processor.
PrivacyPage.recipientProvidersBody: Such as our accountant and IT support, only where they need access to do their work.
PrivacyPage.recipientCounterpartLabel: Parties to your case and authorities.
PrivacyPage.recipientCounterpartBody: Courts, opposing parties and their lawyers, bailiffs, notaries, experts, the Bar and public authorities, including the tax authorities, where acting for you or the law requires it.
PrivacyPage.recipientsBody2: Processors act only on our instructions and under a written agreement. Disclosure to anyone else happens only with your consent, or where the law requires it.
PrivacyPage.transfersBody: The office keeps personal data within the European Economic Area wherever it can. Some services used by this website, in particular the Google Maps frame and our host, a US company, may process data outside the EEA. Where that happens it takes place under the safeguards Chapter V GDPR requires, such as an adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses. In a case with a foreign element, data goes to a foreign court, authority or lawyer only as far as that specific matter requires.
PrivacyPage.retentionIntro: Personal data is kept no longer than its purpose requires. In practice:
PrivacyPage.retentionFilesBody: Five years after the engagement ends, as the rules on lawyers’ files provide, and longer where the law or a dispute that is still going on requires it.
PrivacyPage.retentionAccountingBody: Accounting records for ten years after the end of the financial year, and identification records under the anti money laundering rules for ten years after the business relationship ends.
PrivacyPage.retentionEnquiryLabel: Enquiries that do not become a matter.
PrivacyPage.retentionEnquiryBody: Up to one year, so we can recognise a conflict of interest if you return, then deleted.
PrivacyPage.retentionConsentBody: Six months, after which we ask again.
PrivacyPage.securityBody: The website is served over an encrypted connection. Files are open only to those who need them for the work, and everyone working for the office is bound by confidentiality. No system is perfect. If a breach ever puts your rights at serious risk, we will inform you and the Data Protection Authority as the GDPR requires.
PrivacyPage.automatedBody: The office takes no decision about you by automated means alone. Whether the office can act for you, and any advice you receive, is decided by an advocate.
PrivacyPage.rightsIntro: Under the GDPR you can ask us to:
PrivacyPage.rightAccessBody: Tell you whether we hold data about you, and give you a copy.
PrivacyPage.rightRectifyBody: Correct data that is wrong or incomplete.
PrivacyPage.rightEraseBody: Delete data, where no legal duty and no legal claim requires us to keep it.
PrivacyPage.rightRestrictBody: Pause the use of data while a dispute about it is resolved.
PrivacyPage.rightPortabilityBody: Hand over, in a machine readable form, the data you gave us on the basis of consent or a contract.
PrivacyPage.rightObjectBody: Stop processing based on our legitimate interests, unless compelling grounds override your objection.
PrivacyPage.rightWithdrawBody: Take back consent you gave, at any time.
PrivacyPage.rightsHowSuffix: . We answer within one month, and may first ask for proof of identity so that we do not hand your data to someone else.
PrivacyPage.rightsLimit: These rights are not absolute. Professional secrecy, a legal retention duty, or the rights of another person can require us to limit a request, and where a case file is concerned that limit is the rule rather than the exception. We always explain what we can.
PrivacyPage.complaintsBody1: If you believe your data is not being handled properly, tell us first so we can put it right. You also have the right to complain to the supervisory authority:
PrivacyPage.complaintsBody2: Complaints about the conduct of an advocate can also be addressed to the President of the Bar of the judicial district of Antwerp.
PrivacyPage.changesBody: This statement carries a version number and a date. When it changes materially we publish the new version here, and where the change concerns something you consented to, we ask for your consent again.
PrivacyPage.supportNote: This statement covers this website and the way the office handles personal data in client matters.
